utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Alex Demirdjian, and Thomas Laugel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And for the Defence. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, it's Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness -- the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning again to you, Dr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: May I remind that you you're still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Welcome back, Dr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. It's a pleasure to see you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good to see you too. Now, during our --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could have P370, please, brought up, which I believe is a Prosecution tab but I don't have the tab number at hand. In any event, the exhibit number is P370.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this was the document that we were discussing when you last left us a couple of weeks ago, Dr. Nielsen. And during our last exchange of question and answer I was asking you whether this document, which just to remind ourselves is a -- some kind of an instruction or an order, guidance, from the 1st Proletarian Guards Division to unidentified -- an unidentified town command, and we see there's a blank there. It could be a form being sent to several town commands or just one town command. It's not very clear. In any event, the signatory is Mico Delic who's the -- a major-general, and he's the commander apparently of the 1st Proletarian Guards Division, and we were discussing this document and I asked you whether this document reflected at least Mico Delic's view that it was necessary to put in place a procedure to permit the occupation of abandoned houses in order, as a means, of maintaining law and order. And you answered in response to that question that that was the hope of some JNA officers as reflected in this document, and I quote you: "That the establishment of such procedures could slow down if not eliminate illegal expulsions," and that's at page 2597. So just to wrap this up, you would agree that at least as far as this document goes, it does reflect an attempt to ensure an orderly occupation of abandoned houses; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And I think the two key parts of this document are the four questions which are posed at the outset of the document, which show what everyone is concerned about at this time. And also the -- at least in the B/C/S, it is the second-to-last paragraph where they talk about the need to maintain public order, security of the citizens, and that they should not under any circumstances permit the harassment or mistreatment of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Right. And you testified previously that the reason for this was that there was a large influx of Western Slavonian refugees who were putting pressure on local authorities, and they were in fact harassing local residents on some occasions, and as you put it this was creating a "a very volatile situation." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is certainly the picture that forms when we review the newest documents that were provided by Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we look at page 2 of the English, which I think is still going to be on page one of the B/C/S, we see sort of a three-tiered decision-making process being laid out here by Major-General Delic. And what he says is in the first instance the authority to determine which abandoned houses are to be occupied by whom should, in the first instance, "be fully transferred to the municipal organs of authority wherever they exist and then where no such municipal organs exist an opinion should be obtained from the commissioner of the municipality." And let me just stop there. Would you agree that there appears there to be a distinction between, on the one hand, saying that transfer the decision making process, if possible, to the local authority, but on the other hand where there's no local authority seek the opinion, the advice, consultation, with the commissioner of the -- of the municipality. Is that a distinction that you see in the B/C/S as well?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think both as concerns the English translation and the B/C/S original, there is a mistake in your question. Because you said in your question that where no such municipal organs exist an opinion should be obtained from the commissioner of the municipality. As I read it, it says if no such commissioner exists for the specific municipality then an opinion is to be obtained from the government of the Serb region or district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, if we take the whole paragraph what I see this paragraph as saying is: If there is a local authority in place, transfer the decision to them. If no local authority, then in the first instance seek the opinion of the commissioner, and where there's -- if there's no commissioner then seek the opinion of the district government. Is that right or do you think I'm misreading that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think we agree that it's a three-step process.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Right. And the distinction that I was drawing your attention to was, on the one hand, if there's a local municipal civil organ they should essentially take care of it. But on the other hand, where there's no such local authority, merely seek the opinion of the commissioner, and in the absence of a commissioner, the district government.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is there a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. And I think, just so I don't forget it, that among the 370 or so documents that we obtained from Belgrade, given that this document, if I recall from the top, it's from the 23rd of December, 1991, that it might be very instructive at some point today to also look at the letter that was sent on the very same day to the military by Mr. Hadzic and to which a response was given by the military on the 25th of December, 1991. Those two documents are among the new documents and in fact deal with precisely this matter. That is, the relationship between the civilian authority, the military authorities, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that as far as this document is concerned, the implication is that if there is no local municipal organ of authority, it's still up to the town commands to make the final decision on settlement of abandoned houses?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we agreed, there is a three-step process which culminates in if the -- if there are no civilian organs of authority available from the municipality and if there's no commissioner, step two, available for the specific municipality, then an opinion is to be obtained from the government of the Serb district.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Right. And now I'm trying to discuss with you the implications of that, and what I'm suggesting to you is that even if you've then gone -- let's assume there is no municipal organ, the town command goes to the commissioner, seeks advice, receives some kind of suggestions, but then, at that point, in the absence of any local organs, it's for the town command to execute the decision and make the decision ultimately as to who goes into which houses; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And in fact even the next paragraph, we see that even where the process of letting abandoned houses is actually assumed by the local organs, the municipal civil organs, you'll see there that it says: "Town commands should ensure, regardless of who issues the decision, and especially if the commands do so," -- now just to divert there, it doesn't specifically say town commands, "... and especially if the commands do so, that the houses allotted to refugees from other areas to move in, even on a temporary basis, are first and foremost of those who will most certainly not come back because of the crimes they committed." Now would you agree that this seems to reflect that the town commands are supposed to exercise some ultimate and final authority, even over decisions of the municipal organs in this respect?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would agree, as I've stated previously, that this is an attempt to impose a modicum of order and organisation upon what has, based on other documents, been a quite chaotic process. So again, the town commands at this point are being told by the major-general that they are supposed to -- to the best of their ability regulate this to prevent the kind of irregularities that have been witnessed to date. The emphasis is, of course, on permitting the return, as we see in the final -- or following paragraph, rather, permitting the return of persons who were loyal and who have not compromised themselves, which gets back to the four questions that are asked at the outset of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we look at the top of page 2 of the English it says, and this is in response to the four questions on page one, it says: "We have received the following reply from the command of the 1st Military District." And then that reply is purportedly set out in this document. Would you agree with me that that seems to imply that this document reflects the policy that in fact is going to apply in all of the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly the aspiration of the command of the 1st Military District in issuing this reply. They, of course, also note that they hope that the -- whatever organs of local authority and police might exist in these municipalities will assist in preventing, as it says at the bottom of the document, any eventual harassment of citizens by those organs or their employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's right. And the second-last paragraph in this document, which is on page three of the English, specifically says: "Town commands are particularly responsible for ensuring law and order, security and safety of citizens." Does that bear out what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And again as we discussed in January, that is to take place in so far as possible with whatever existing local organs of civilian authority, including the police, do exist in such municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But this document is saying, Whatever the case may be, you shall ensure these conditions; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But, again, that is not to say that the sole responsibility for doing so was on the military. From this and other documents it is clear, again, we talked about this transitional process in January, where power local authority is gradually being established in various municipalities where it has been absent because of armed conflict. The military is observing a lot of irregularities. In many cases, unfortunately, those irregularities include harassment of civilians or removal of civilians that is being perpetrated by the police, so to the extent that all of these irregularities are occurring, the military at this point is still very keen to say: All other things equal, we have a strong obligation to prevent such irregularities; we have a strong obligation to implement a sense of public order and peace; and if it is possible to do so, we do it in cooperation with municipal and civilian authorities; if not, we still have to do it because no one else is going to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And as we discussed at the very beginning of your testimony, one of the reasons we're looking at these JNA documents at all is that they reflect events on the ground. So would you agree that when we see the JNA here saying that this shall be done, that the force -- the town commands should ensure this reflects that they perceive the need to fulfil that role; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I apologise to the court reporter for speaking so rapidly. I agree with you. There is a -- I can only say an irony present here because, again, the available documentation suggests that the military would very much like to transfer responsibility for these matters to the -- to the civilian authorities, including the police. However, the documents produced by the military, including by the 1st Command here, suggest -- or 1st Military District, suggest that in many cases the police, where they did exist, or the civilian authorities, where they did exist, or the district authorities, where they did exist, were unfortunately involved in the type of harassments of citizens and the removal of citizens that the military is keen to prevent here. So the question - and we see this expressed by the military in some cases - is how do we go about fulfilling our aspiration of transferring authority to the civilian authorities when those civilian authorities are, at least in part, engaged in behaviour which we want to prevent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it may come as no surprise to you that I reject the claim that this was a function of activities by the district authorities, and we're going to come back to some documents to address that. But what I'm driving at now is would you agree that this document appears to reflect that the only force capable of ensuring law and order in these areas shortly after significant combat operations, the only authority able to do that is the JNA; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we're going in circles a bit here. But, yes, I agree that the military is essentially positioning itself as -- as it were, the guarantor of peace as a last resort. If the other organs are not in place, then the military, as I've said, still has a role to provide for the security of civilians and to prevent these irregularities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So, therefore, this suggests that the other organs are not in place; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have stated repeatedly --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, if you can answer the question yes or no, all of your answers are on the record. I do understand the nuances that you are placing on this, and the Judges I'm sure will as well, and the Prosecution can follow it up, but now I'm just asking you that specific question.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a question that can be answered by yes or no. The briefest answer is that it varied from municipality to municipality at this time as we can see in the documentation, so the answer to your question is yes, this suggests that in some municipalities the other organs are not in place and therefore the military has to perform their role.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P371, please, which is Prosecution tab 350.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, you've addressed this document before, Dr. Nielsen, so I'm not going to go through it in its entirety. I just have a couple of specific issues that I'd like to draw your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could turn over to page 2 of the English. And just for context, this is dated 25th of December, 1991. It's from Colonel Belic who is the commander of the Ilok town command addressed the 1st Guards Brigade Command. And on page 2 we see here, in English, it probably is on page 1 of the English, that in Ilok there are 800 vacant houses and flats. Do you have any indication as to whether that is a approximately accurate number or inaccurate number?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information at present that would allow me to verify or doubt that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then it says: "About 150 have been moved into, without authorisation, which will be emptied in the coming period and planned and organised settlement will be required." Would you agree that what seems to be going on here is that Colonel Belic is saying that some people have moved into these houses without the JNA giving what they consider the appropriate permission, and they are now going to go into these houses, remove the people that are there, and then resettle with new individuals. Is that -- does that seem to be what is envisioned?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be what is envisioned. I would also point out that this is the document which, as you noted, we saw previously and at the outset the JNA refers to the fact that unfortunately some of these problems which have emerged are at least in part due to the lack of care of the district authorities of the SAO as stated in the first paragraph, and that is also evident in the letter sent by the JNA command in Ilok on the same day to Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this was the language that you noted as being somewhat obscure about unobjective difficulties and elsewhere, in fact, in -- in very paragraph 1, it refers to what this commander views as the unjustifiable indolence of the district government. Now, leaving aside the pejorative connotations, would you agree that that reflects that there's no indication here that the district government is trying to push aside the JNA's role in Ilok?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, that's all spelled out much more clearly in that exchange of correspondence between Mr. Hadzic and the Ilok town command and the 23rd and 25th of December 1991. Speaking on the totality of the new documents obtained from Belgrade, it seems to me a reasonable observation to state that what the JNA command is hinting at here is something stated explicitly in other documents, which is that a number of persons linked to the government of the district were allegedly - and I state allegedly because this is -- I have not been able to verify this, but this is what is stated in the military documents - had allegedly been involved in the removal of citizens from their homes in some of these municipalities. So perhaps that is what the author of this document is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It appears from this document indeed that they consider permits issued by the district government to be unauthorised or improper. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very interesting question because it goes back to the very first document you showed me in January from Srboljub Trajkovic where he is actually struggling with the question of whether he is supposed to regard the SAO district as legitimate -- a legitimate organ of authority or not. So as of this date, at least at some levels or at some times they're still struggling with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely my point, Dr. Nielsen. When I read this document, and you can tell me whether you disagree or agree, agree in part, when I read this document I get the impression that Colonel Belic seems to view the district authorities with a certain level of contempt and he does not appear to recognise that any permits that may have been issued by the district government are, to him, valid.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be the case for Ilok. As I would again note in the correspondence to which I refer, there is kind of a, for lack of a better term, a dance between the military and Mr. Hadzic in which they both assure each other of their highest mutual respect and desire for co-operation but both, explicitly in the case of the military and implicitly a bit in Mr. Hadzic's letter, suggest that they have not been entirely on the same wavelength as regards this and other issues, and hopefully that can be -- those kinds of difficulties and disagreements can be eliminated in the period to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I mean, the reason that I -- and what I draw your attention to specifically is that second last paragraph in the document which is -- starts on page 3 of the English and goes over to page 4, and what the document says is: "Unauthorised settlement of Ilok is widespread, although this command, i.e., this town command, has not issued a single permit. There is no point describing -- in describing the various cases, but this might have been done by SAO ministers Bogunovic and Ljubo Loncarevic, a former policeman who is now in Backa Palanka, and on so." So what Belic appears to be saying is, here we have permits allegedly issued by Minister Bogunovic. He seems to consider such permits unauthorised.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 6063, which is Prosecution tab 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this appears to be some sort of a response to this previous letter or correspondence from Colonel Belic. And this is from the Serbian district government -- well, it doesn't say government. Serbian district of SBWS, ministry of justice and administration, and the date there is the 29th of December, 1991, and the place is mentioned as Ilok. Now I first of all want to ask you, is this the first document - and I put it to you that this is the case - the first document for anyone associated with the district government that actually appears to originate from the town of Ilok?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no ability to answer that question. I would have to look at the -- all the documents to reach that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you go with my characterisation that it seems to be some kind of a reaction or response to the issues, if not directly the document, at least the issues that are being raised by Colonel Belic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And as I noted, there is a desire to have better co-ordination henceforth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to make sure, is my learned friend tendering the cover page or the whole -- because it's a -- it's a bundle of about 30 or 40 pages with annexes, from my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, this -- the entire document is being tendered -- proposed for tendering by the Prosecution; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We didn't propose it, but we're perfectly happy to have it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, then I would suggest for simplicity that we -- and we do tender the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a document which will be dealt also with our -- another expert, so the substance of it will be discussed. There are tables attached to it which show figures, I believe, on the movement of population and the number of people left per ethnic group before and after the conflict. So I don't know if it is appropriate at this time to deal with it with this witness. But in any case they can be admitted and another witness will look at the substance of the annexes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, perhaps it'd be simplest just to tender the cover page. Needless to say, the Defence doesn't necessarily accept the reliability of all the figures in the annex. This is purely a matter of convenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you are tendering the cover page only; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If that is logistically possible from the Registry perspective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for having added a complication to the matter, but essentially I think that the document does not make sense if it's broken apart. The record reflects what Dr. Neilsen has said about it. And this, as far as the document itself, I don't think would make sense to remove the cover letter separately without the supporting document, so I think the whole document can come in, and the record reflects what Dr. Nielsen has said and other witnesses may comment later on as to the substance of the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We just came to the conclusion that it would be best to upload this document again and admit it then as such separately. Would that be convenient?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perfectly appropriate as far as we're concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you'll upload the document again, separately, Mr. Gosnell, and, for the moment, it is admitted and marked for identification for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first page of 65 ter document 6063 shall be assigned Exhibit D28, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar. Could we have P372, which is Prosecution tab 361.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is a letter from something called the central settlement committee, which appears to be part of the district government of SBWS. And it's dated the 11th of February, 1992. And you -- you did comment on this document during your previous testimony, so again I'm not going to go through it chapter and verse. But somehow the Prosecution didn't ask you about paragraph 2 of this document, and you didn't have a chance to specifically comment upon it. And paragraph 2 says -- and this appears to be some kind of advice or instruction to a particular commune, Mohovo, and what it says is: "We would like to inform you that the government of the Serbian district did not adopt any decisions regarding the moving out of persons of Croatian nationality from the territory of the Serbian district because it is more than obvious that the mere fact of whether or not someone is a Croat or a member of another nationality doesn't represent sufficient grounds for withholding from them the right to stay or reside in the territory of the Serbian district." Would you agree that that appears to reflect that individuals should not be harassed or forcibly removed based on ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is what the document says. However, as an analytical observation, it raises the question of whether we can take this document at its face value given that the previous documents we looked at seemed to indicate that at some -- at some level, the district had been involved in perhaps not moving out of -- persons out of Croatian nationality but moving persons in of Serbian nationality, and in the totality of the documentation, particularly the new military documentation from Serbia that I've been able to review, there seemed to be indications in other documents that such moving out of persons of Croatian nationality did take place. But, yes, at -- this document in its third paragraph has a clear statement prohibiting the harassment or forcible removal of persons based on their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, in terms of the reliability of the content of this document as an indication of actual policy, one of the points that you made during your previous testimony was that documents that don't have wide circulation that are not going out to the public for public consumption, you would say are entitled to all else being equal a higher level of reliability. And wouldn't you agree that this document is just going from the central settlement committee to one commune?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is true that -- that it is only go to the local commune. However, I analytically treat this document quite differently than a document of the Serbian State Security Service which is what we were looking at earlier, which is state secret or at least -- at the very least an official secret. This is a document that bears no stamp of confidentiality and there is no indication here that anything in this document was designed to be kept confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then in the third paragraph, or the fourth paragraph depending on how you count, you will see that what they're saying is that individuals who -- that individuals could in fact be deprived of their residency on two conditions: If there is "reliable information that they've collaborated with the enemy and Ustasha authorities; and 2, if it is established that their actions are still motivated by such positions and beliefs." Now, would you say that that's also consistent with the position apparently being taken by the JNA in other documents that you've seen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does seem to be consistent with the position taken by the JNA. I would again note that the key word in what you just read is "reliable." And in this very difficult and very tense environment after the period of armed conflict, the indications that I have seen from documents are that not a lot of energy was being devoted to verifying the reliability of allegations that someone of Croat ethnicity had been assisting the Croat authorities and that, unfortunately, led to a number of incidents in which people were attacked or removed from their places of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that -- I mean, aren't you mixing apples and oranges there, Dr. Nielsen? I mean, one thing is to say that when -- that individuals of Croatian ethnicity were just attacked as a matter of lawlessness, including by this large number of Western Slavonian refugees who you described as creating a very volatile situation. It wasn't as if those attacks were -- followed some sort of quasi-judicial examination by municipal authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that there was unfortunately no procedure, as far as I've been able to tell, put in place to verify the veracity of those allegations and therefore a number of people were subjected to arbitrary treatment on the basis of such allegations. And I would also agree with you that this document, which is being issued in April -- in February 1992, aspires to prevent such things from occurring and notes that the mere fact that someone is of Croatian nationality is not sufficient to justify their expulsion from the territory of the Serbian district. Indications are that from the military documentation that by this point, of course, the number of Croats left in the area is much smaller than it was in November or December of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that because a large number of Croats had left simultaneous with the military operations?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military documents indicate that, indeed, a very large number of Croats left either prior to military operations or during the military operations. The military documents also indicate that in a number of cases those -- that minority of Croats who did stay after military operations had ceased were in some cases forced to leave or were unable to stay because of the circumstances to which I have referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you agree that this document appears to suggest that decision-making in individual cases resides at the commune level?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems to be the indication. And I would point out that the newly available documentation actually includes lists of non-Serbs; that is, not just Croat, also but Hungarians, Slovaks, Ruthenians, in which those individuals are listed with comments made by local authorities assessing their loyalty to the newly established authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that dove-tail with Prosecution Exhibit 370, which was the one from the 1st Military District where they appear to place primary importance on co-operation with commune authorities in terms of settlement?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, to the extent that one accepts the legitimacy of an exercise, the point of which is to assess the loyalty of people, then the prevailing assumption was that the local authorities knew who everybody was and therefore were better placed to assess the loyalty of those persons than persons several -- authorities several rungs up the ladder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I don't propose to explore with you the broader implications of the process itself, and I think that you've said that that wouldn't be within the realm of your expertise so I don't propose to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 6094 which is Prosecution tab 362, please. And I believe, do I understand that to be under -- not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document has been already admitted as Exhibit P329 under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this document appears to be from the 1st Mechanised Corps Command from the assistant commander for civilian affairs, Colonel Novica Gusic, and he appears to be based in Principovac which, I don't know if you know this, but is just over the border in Serbia not far from Ilok. And if we go to page 3 of the English, which is about the eighth paragraph of the document, Dr. Nielsen. I'm not sure if that would make it on page 1 or on page 2. And it says: "At the end of the presentation, the president of the local commune opened the debate, which reached the conclusion that there were two factions in the village: One, Serbs from Western Slavonia; and, two, Serbs, locals, who worked to protect Croats." Now would you again view this as a further indication that there was this tension or cleavage between refugees moving into the area and local people, including local authorities, who had a much more protective view of their Croatian neighbours?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this is actually an excellent indication of a broader phenomenon that we also see in Bosnia, which is that local residents, all other things equal, are more tolerant of continued co-existence with their long-standing neighbours of other ethnicity and that often the appearance of outsiders, some of whom have, of course, been radicalised in their views on multi-ethnic co-existence by the fact that they were themselves expelled from other areas in Yugoslavia plays in, and so we see that the long-standing local inhabitants, which are also often referred to in military documents, actually try to insist that whatever Croats, Hungarian, et cetera, may remain on the territory of the commune or the municipality should be permitted to stay. I should also note, however, though, that the previous paragraph right before the one you read is quite interesting given that this was the same local commune that issued a decision to change the name of the village into Arkanovo, which seems to be somewhat indicative of their views of Mr. Raznjatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well perhaps it suggests that those two sentiments are not completely incompatible.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That to me would be a complete non sequitur, but -- given what is known about the behaviour of Mr. Raznjatovic in this area, but certainly shows the respect in which he was held by some of the local inhabitants and, indeed, at times also by some members of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now on page 4 of the English, and this is the part that I'm particularly interested in, and the English paragraph starts, "Having listened...," so I think it's about five paragraphs from the bottom, Dr. Nielsen, and it says: "Having listened to their discussion and debate the PK for CP," and that is that's the assistant commander for civilian affairs, so in other words that's the author of this document, "Having listened to their discussion and debate the PK for CP assigned assign-posts and specific tasks in the establishment and functioning of the civilian authorities, the organisation and formation of TO units, and instructed them in the method of resolving all the problems cited, emphasising in particular ..." And then it goes on to identify three aspects in particular: "The settlement and evacuation committee," the need for newly formed organs of the civilian authorities to organise life in the village including "securing housing and food for people," and 3, "form a TO and police force unit as soon as possible and build the security of the village, the safety of individuals, and the implementation of legal decisions on that foundation." Now we've seen other documents that reflect the same theme, but just to ask you again: Does this reflect that there are few, if any, of these institutions up and running and that the town command or the JNA officer for civilian protection, civilian affairs, is taking a lead role in ensuring that those organisation -- organs are set up?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P373, which is Prosecution tab 363.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is a fairly high-level document. It emanates from the 1st Mechanised Corps Command. It's dated the 16th of February 1992. So it's from the 1st Mechanised Corps Command to the Military District, and it's from the assistant commander for civilian affairs to the corresponding organ for civilian affairs at the 1st Military District, so I would just suggest that this is a fairly high-level document going from the corps to the Military District. And you did look at this document during your testimony. But one paragraph that you did not address during that testimony is on page 2 of the English, the last full paragraph: "It is indicative that in many cases the relocated Serbs wished to impose their will on long-time residents and to control decision making and power. In someplace -- places there have been unsolved murders and pressure to have the Croatian population move out regardless of whether they are loyal or involved in the Croatian Defence Forces." Now, again, do you see that there -- appears to be in this document as well a recognition of that distinction between refugees moving in and the local population, in terms of their attitudes towards Croats?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on page 4, under point 4, it says that -- there's an allegation. It says: "Relocated persons have been putting great pressure on the local population because they are inciting the relocation of the Croatian population and of other nationalities. They state that there can be no co-existence there and that they should be relocated and treated like the Croats treated the Serbs. Their incitement has the tacit support of all the organs of authority, ranging from the government to the local commune." Now I assume that you would interpret "the government" to mean the district government, would you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. And the district government is, of course, also referred to in the following paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can just turn back to the bottom of page 2 of the English and the top of page 3. And it refers to a very specific problem. It says: "Croatian houses are being occupied and their property is being misappropriated. There are frequent instances of relocated Serb families occupying two or three houses per family. CP," that is civilian affairs, "organs of the 1st Mechanised Corps in co-operation with the town commands, local commune executive councils, and the police are making great effort to prevent such situations." Now do you note that there is a contradiction there. On the one hand he is saying, on pages 2 to 3, the police and the local commune authorities are making great efforts to prevent such situations. And then, over on page 4, he says, their incitement, i.e., the incitement of these refugees who are putting pressure on the Croats, their incitement has the tacit support of all the organs of authority ranging from the government to the local commune. Can you explain how in the same document the author can express two such apparently contradictory opinions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that these are only contradictory opinions if we assume that the authorities to which the author refers are monolithic, which they are definitely not. In all of the authorities we have the local commune in, for example, Bapska, which we also saw earlier, where there is an evident power struggle ongoing between the long time residents and the newly arrived persons, perhaps those are the persons who are pushing for the renaming of the commune, and in the police where there were police officers who had worked there for decades. It was the area in which they had grown up and had their entire professional lives, but there were also police officers who had arrived more recently, some of them from Western Slavonia as well, some of them from Serbia or even Montenegro, in some cases, or Bosnia, as well as, of course, the presence of paramilitary forces and various ill-defined nebulous police forces that seemed to be roaming the area and making appearances here and there during this period. So I read this document as a rather accurate reflection of a situation, a very dynamic situation of the type that we discussed in January in which there are certainly a number of the police and a number of the local residents and a number of the local authorities, including probably also members of the district government who wish to prevent such situations, but there are others who are actually and actively contributing to creating these problems that are deplored in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you agree that this diversity of attitudes is possible because the institutions of power, at least on the civilian side, are rather weak?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. And, unfortunately, it seems to be the case that in some municipalities and communes in this period, decisions were taken with a view to protecting Croats, Hungarian, Ukrainians, and others, but those decisions were then overturned or counteracted violently by those forces who enjoyed superiority of fire-power.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that in some cases individuals simply appropriated titles for themselves and said, I am now this or that, I'm holding this or that office, and on the basis of this or that authority I'm going to engage in such activities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are such instances. I would point to one of the military documents that became available in which a person is said to have suddenly proclaimed himself to be, and I quote, "an idol" for the local municipality and asks that everyone treat him as an idol and obey his decisions, despite the fact that he has barely finished secondary school. And he makes a number of decisions which the military view as ill-informed, violent, and completely counter-productive to the maintenance of co-existence between various nationalities. Again, such instances are -- are to be found in the documentation. It is unfortunately the case that after the civilian authorities are established one can find little trace of any effort to actually rectify those wrongs that were committed or to prosecute those persons who arbitrarily asserted such authority and made such decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's take a more pedestrian example than someone declaring themselves an idol, and in fact it's on this very page, and I consider it very significant because it refers to someone who is alleged to be a part of the district government. And you've been referring to allegations of misfeasance and criminal behaviour by such individuals. And it says: "There are also self-proclaimed representatives of the SAO government and the secret police has been appearing, but it is difficult to determine their legitimacy. We have one example in particular. The Serbian police group has been staying in the sector of Bapska village, the wine cellar, and Marko Loncarevic, aka Chetnik, has been introducing himself as the minister of defence of the government and is arming the relocated Serbs with the aim of forming his own groups and detachments." Now, sir, I assume that you know, having looked at the documents, that Ilija Kojic is the minister of defence in the SBWS at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any documents suggesting that Marko Loncarevic had a position in the Ministry of Defence of the district government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Wouldn't you expect the author of this document to be fully aware that that claim was false by Marko Loncarevic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the author is aware of the falsehood of that claim, he does not make that awareness explicit in this document, but I am sure that the author of this document was quite aware of the situation to which you referred, which is that there were a number of self-proclaimed commanders, leader, et cetera, who were roaming around this area and undertaking such activities at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: One additional observation of interest in this document is over on page 5. It says: "Another fact is that all levels of," presumably, "civilian authority organs from the local commune to the government do not respect each other and are criticising certain solutions and positions." Would you agree that there was a very fractious relationship between various organs of government? And I believe that you've already said this, but I'll put the question to you squarely: Do you think that there was not only a fractious relationship between levels of government but fractious relationships even within the same government institutions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that there were a lot of disagreements and a lot of conflicts between various personalities during this period including in the district government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that of all the documents that we've looked at from the JNA, both today and last time, that there's no indication at all that the JNA, at any time, views itself as subordinate to the district government authorities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have L38, which is Prosecution tab 128. If we could have page 4 of the English, which, I believe, should be near the end of the document. Yes, it is -- it should be on the last page of the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this is the minutes of the 17th Session of the Government of the District of SBWS held on 19th of November in Erdut. And item 5 says -- and these are the conclusions that have been purportedly unanimously adopted at the session. It says: "JNA units are subordinated to the government of the Serbian district on its territory." Have you -- have you seen any evidence that this conclusion was ever communicated to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen any direct evidence that this conclusion was ever communicated to the JNA. I would, again, note that the correspondence almost precisely a month later between Mr. Hadzic and the JNA command in Ilok is, to me, the best indication of the SAO district government and the military trying to actually hash out what their mutual relationship is supposed to be given a number of misunderstandings that have occurred on -- in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, do you have any indication that the JNA subordinated itself, in practice, to the government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no evidence that the JNA subordinated itself in practice to the government based -- pursuant to this decision. Again, it is perhaps, again, necessary for me to underline that I looked primarily at the police organs in the SAO and, therefore, did not specifically focus on this question, and I'm sure the military expert will be able to speak to this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, he might or might not. I think that's speculation at this point. But what's important is that in the realm of police matters where we've seen a great number of JNA documents, and you've looked at them, there is no indication that in respect of those areas the JNA placed itself -- subordinated -- it subordinated itself to the district government; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to your discussion of Arkan, and during your previous testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're done with that document, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: During your previous testimony, at page 2521, you said, and I quote you, quote your words: "That there were training centres that seemed to have been exclusively under the control of organs affiliated with Belgrade." And then at 2522 you identified those two training centres as being the one at Golubic and at Erdut. And then you went on to testify at 2523 that Arkan, in your view, had exclusive control over that training centre because there was a "general perception" that "he was a person who enjoyed the protection and favour of federal or Serbian organ -- of a federal or Serbian organ based in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now could we have P194.140. Which is a Defence document on our list.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you hadn't given the testimony that I just quoted to you when you were shown this document during your direct examination by the Prosecution. But the Prosecution was asking you about how it was possible to reconcile this document with information that Arkan was in the employ of the DB of Serbia. And in the context of that situation, you testified as follows, at page 2509: "I am not certain how I would personally reconcile it other than to simply state that as an analyst this is the documentation that has become available to me and, therefore, I saw fit to include it in my report." Now that answer was -- was interesting to me because it was somewhat different from the answers that you give in respect of some other documents. In respect of some documents you say that you gave theme credence because they were corroborated by other documents, for example, at page 2439 of your testimony; or that they exemplify a general proposition that you know is supported by other documents, and you said that at 2453. So my initial question to you is: Do you have any hesitation or doubts about the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not have any hesitations about the doubts or about the authenticity of this document, and I cite it in footnote 323 of my report on page 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And that's at paragraph 201 of your report, I believe. And what you say there is -- and it is rather unequivocal, I must say: "As noted previously, Goran Hadzic had in September 1991 in his capacity as the president of the government of the SAO SBWS appointed Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, commander of the TO centre in Erdut." And equally unequivocally you then say in the next sentence: "Arkan had until that point served as the commander of special units of the TO of SAO SBWS." Have you -- do you know whether there actually was any such thing known as special -- the -- the TO AO SBWS special forces? Did any such unit exist, to your knowledge, in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would note that the reason I write this in the report in footnote 3 -- and cite this document in footnote 323 is that, first of all, I'm stating what -- what this document says on its face value. Second of all, there are a number of documents, not a lot but I think two or three in the new batch of documents, also that indicate that there were -- that -- that Arkan was commander of the TO of the SAO SBZS as I call it here, SBWS, during this period. So there are references to such special units having existed. I cannot personally verify whether those special units did exist and I have not seen documents generated by those special units if they did generate such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you're saying that there are documents that you've seen that refers to TO special forces in the SBWS prior to the 21st of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They refer to those special forces existing. As to whether they specifically refer to the date of the 21st of September 1991, I cannot state at this present point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, our view is that this document is a forgery. And I want to take you through a few specific elements of this document in comparison with other documents. So to start this process I just want to look, focus on a couple of individual aspects of it. You'll first of all see a reference at the top to the secretariat of the president. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that a formulation, as you sit there now, that you can recall ever having been used in any other document issued by the district government of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall such a formulation having been used elsewhere. I would also point out that as we previously discussed we have very, very few documents from the government as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we see there the number at the top 1/91, and I'll just ask you to take note of that. One thing I noticed about your report was a fairly strange nomenclature that you referred in your footnote to this document. You referred to 65 ter 1D1630. Now that's not a 65 ter number from this case, so where did you get this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this was among the documents that, if not the initial batch of documents, then one of the batches of the documents that was given to me by the Office of the Prosecutor when I started to prepare this report. I recall a small number of such documents had no ERNs but had only 65 ter numbers, including a small number of documents that had 65 ter numbers from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. We're about to turn away from this document, so are you fully familiar with it now that you've had it on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we now have L43, please, which is Prosecution tab 137. Actually, this wasn't the document that I was hoping for. Could we have 65 ter -- 65 ter 00754, which is Prosecution tab 137. Sorry, 65 ter 00754. This is the document? Your Honours, could we take a break and I'll make sure that I have the correct document for you when we return? I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we'll take the first break. We'll come back at 11.00. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in, may I address you with a very small kitchen sink matter. I spoke to my learned friend. I believe he needs the full session now and the third session as well. I was informed that he will try to go as fast as possible, but if needs be would we be capable of sitting an extra half-hour for the purposes of re-examination? As you know, Mr. Nielsen has to fly today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 00248. Which actually is a document that appears in another document that is on the Prosecution list. And I consulted with my learned friend opposite, who has kindly agreed not to object to this one not being on either of our lists. Well, somehow, that, again, is not the right document. So what I'm going to do is bring it up in the document that is listed. It's 01939. That's Prosecution tab 292, and we're looking for page 63 of the English. It should be approximately page 226 of the B/C/S. Perhaps page 225. Yes, this is it. It's under -- under item 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I understand from your report you do refer to this -- to this document at footnote 51 of your report. And you generally consider the documents that are included in Mr. Petrovic's book to be authentic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in those cases where I have been able to examine the documents because the OTP also possesses other versions of them. They corroborate what are put in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's quite right in respect of this document. I was trying to put you to the gazetted version. In any event the form is the same. But I draw your attention there to the number. It says log number 1/91? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we go down to the next page in English. And if we can go to the subsequent page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you'll see that Mr. Hadzic signs as prime minister, that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can just go back now to the top of this document, which is two pages prior. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now you'll see there that there is no reference to the secretariat of the president. He refers -- or the heading of the document is "prime minister"; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although I would point out just so we are clear on this that the term "prime minister" in B/C/S can also be translated into English as "president of the government."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's quite right. I thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we now move to 00261; Prosecution tab 88.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just to follow up on that last question, it doesn't say the office of the prime minister or the secretariat of the prime minister, does it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision on the implementation of regulations. And the number given to this document is you see down -- the date is the 30th of August, 1991. Before the date it says, "in Dalj." And the number given is a quadruple-barrelled number 02-3-2/1-1991. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you consider this document in its form and content to be authentic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D29. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now the next document in chronological order is P19410 [sic], which is the document in question that we're most concerned with. It's P194.140.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, in this case you will see the secretariat of the president, and we see the number 1/91. We saw that number in the second-last document, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this document is now coming the 21st of September, 1991, which is approximately three weeks after the -- the previous document we looked at, which was on the 20 -- the 30th of August, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you'll see that there isn't any quadruple-barrelled numbering in terms of the tracking number of this document; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P260.253, which is Defence tab 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is the -- is the next document in our chronology of district government documents. There's no number here. It's left blank apparently. This comes six days after the -- the vital document that we're focussing on. And you'll see that the nomenclature used is not the secretariat of the president but the secret of the government; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. There was a secretariat of the government and in the page you showed me earlier from the gazette of the district, the secretary -- you mean the secretariat of the government was also referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you for that information. And, at the bottom we see someone signing for the prime minister, Mr. Hadzic, and then there's a signature; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that it is someone signing for Mr. Hadzic. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: May we have P196.14 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just before we leave this document, and this is a technical matter, I'm not sure whether you've captured it. But this is after the constitution has been promulgated and the name of the SBWS has changed to the Serbian District instead of the Serbian Autonomous District, and you'll note that they've left the name "autonomous" in there. Would you agree that that's simply a mistake on their part?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many such mistakes. They were not particularly meticulous in their attention to such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could have P196.140, which is Defence tab 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gosnell, excuse me. Before showing us another document, I would like to a question to the witness. Witness, you have studied the different institutions, and is it possible to have, on the one hand, a secretariat of the government and on the other hand a secretariat of the president of the government? Is that possible? Because you've done quite a few research. Did you notice this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But did you find any examples? Because you have -- you have analysed several texts. If I understood well, this is what Mr. Gosnell is doing now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour. That is precisely what the exercise that we're going through now. I have, however, not, as I responded to Mr. Gosnell, seen a significant number of documents issued by the secretariat of the president of the president of the government, whereas I have seen a significant number of documents issued by the secretariat of the government. Again, unfortunately the state of documentation that we have from the district authorities is very incomplete, and I cannot conclude based on the available documents whether a secretariat of the president of the government existed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It is very clear and I will not ask you any further question about this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is P196.140 in front of us. It's dated 2 October 1991. It appears to be a decision. It's number 1/91. And if we can scroll over to page 2, or perhaps just the bottom of the page, we'll see that it's signed by the prime minister, Goran Hadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And if I may be so bold as to jump ahead and, as I can clearly see where this is going, there are a number of documents with the registration number 1/91. There are, of course, a number of different institutions within the district that exist and some of those have sub-offices. It is entirely consistent with the operation of government authorities that each such office has at least one set of registration numbers, sometimes more than one, and, therefore, different entities within the government are able to issue numbers with the registration number 1/91.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But these are all coming from the prime minister, Mr. Hadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close examination of these documents indicates that the letterhead on these various documents is not identical. There are deferences in nomenclature, which mean that even though the signatory may be Mr. Hadzic, he can be signing documents that are issued by various units, as it were, of the authorities of the district.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's go back to the top of the page, please. This is coming from the government of the Serbian District of SBWS; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. And if memory serves, one of the previous documents we saw, which also had the number 1/91, was also issued by the government of the Serbian district of the SBWS but, in that case, was -- the header also included the words "secretariat of the government."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes. Just so you understand and we all understand now, we don't place great reliance on the numbering. It's a factor that may be of interest, relevance. What we do place reliance on is the anomalous reference to the secretariat of the president which is found on one and only one of these various documents, the one in question. I'm just letting you know that now. That's not a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we go on to the next document, which is P251.245. P251.245, which is Defence tab 52. And I believe it's not to be broadcast. This document is signed by the prime minister, Goran Hadzic. And here we see a reference to the government secretariat again. There's no number. And it's Dalj, the 16th of October, 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you have no reason to believe, based on its form or content, that this is not an authentic document, do you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is probably a copy of a document and it is somewhat odd that there's no number issued for this order, but I have no reason to doubt that it's authentic. Again, for the reason that they were not very meticulous in issuing such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: It's not the only document without a number, though, is it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And, in fact, you can also find documents without numbers that are issued on, for example, non-existing dates, such as the 31st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have L43, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is your report at tab -- at footnote 60, so it's a Prosecution document on their list. And, again, this is a decision signed by the president of the government, Goran Hadzic, and it -- it appears to involve the appointment of an individual to an Executive Council of a municipality. And you'll see there the number 0 -- again, we see this quadruple-barrelled formulation, 02-3-25/1-1991. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P51, which is Defence tab 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 21st of January, 1992, again signed by Mr. Hadzic. And again we see that quadruple-barrelled formulation. And it appears to involve some kind of facilitating the operationalisation of an activity plan to establish civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I don't think we have the right document on the screen. We have a list of the members of the SDS here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's not what it should be. Is this P51? Well, I'm going to have to skip that one and I'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand that your position is that the documentation that comes out of the government is, in relative terms, relative to, for example, the Republika Srpska, is sparse, but here we have a half-dozen or so documents that are decisions signed by Goran Hadzic as the prime minister. Sometimes there's not always a reference to the government, although there usually is a reference to the government. Sometimes there is a secretariat of the government referred to, I think in two of the documents. But I put it to you that in none of these documents, and actually there are more, in none of these documents that are produced from the period between August and early 1992, is there ever a reference to the secretariat of the president? Now I know that you don't have all the documents at your fingertips, but would agree that that level of anomaly is at least significant in assessing the authenticity of the document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am happy to agree with you that I have not been able to view any other documents issued from a secretariat of the president, and that given that the document cited in footnote 323 is, to date, the only document that refers to such a secretariat, that should be taken into consideration in considering the reliability and authenticity of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you didn't mention that in your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I did not mention any concerns about the reliability or authenticity of that document in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 1D186, please, which is Defence tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, we in the Defence wrote to the government of Serbia to see whether they had this document anywhere in their archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I'm not sure whether we need to be in private session, but perhaps we ought to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now what I put to you, Dr. Nielsen, just to put a conclusion on this discussion, is you have an anomalous - and we say flatly erroneous - reference to the secretariat of president. We have a reference to what we say is a unit that doesn't exist. You have a reference to Arkan being the commander of that non-existent unit, whereas he never was such a commander. You have a potentially, although we wouldn't place much reliance on this, errant reference number, and when you look at that altogether, and then we will be discussing some contextual factors as well, when you put all that together combined with an absence for the origin for this document, does all that give you any pause as to whether this -- you should have wrote -- you should have given what I say is implicit credence in your report that this is all true?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to separate my answer into two parts. The first part is a direct response to your question. The second part is a more general observation which, with the Court's permission, I think we would have to discuss in closed session. But the first part which I can deal with in open session is to state that I agree with you that there are many points that you raise which are valid concerning the possible credibility of this document. And those are things that I hope that you and the Court will take into consideration in weighting this document compared to other available documentation. I would, however, point out that in the totality of documents that I have been able to review, we do have a very interesting document from November 1991 from General Biorcevic, who was based in Novi Sad, in which he issues a -- I believe it is a machine-gun as a present to Mr. Raznjatovic, and in that particular document in issuing the gun to Mr. Raznjatovic, Mr. Biorcevic or General Biorcevic states that Arkan had held this function as a commander of the TO of the district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and he also refers to special forces. So that's one document that should also be taken into consideration. As for whether I should address the second more general point, again, we would need to go into closed session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter -- I'm now finished with that document and I'm going to move on to a new subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you moving to another topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to get this document. Ask Mr. Nielsen -- Dr. Nielsen, we are discussing at length now the word "president" and "secretariat of the president" here. President, government president, that's -- those are the terms on -- on the -- the words on this document. But you said that in B/C/S there might be a similarity. Could you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My -- my only point was to make sure that everyone understands that the term "prime minister" in English in B/C/S is most often "predsednik vlade" which literally means president of the government. In this case, on the B/C/S original, Mr. Hadzic's name and signature appear below the Serbian words "president of the government." That is in the vast majority of cases the term that would be used to refer to a prime minister. In this case, if and - I stress if - a secretariat of the president did exist, then it would in this case seem to refer to not a president but to the secretariat of the president of the government, i.e., the president -- the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And is -- are these words in this document, in B/C/S, different in an important way from all the others we've seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is nothing in the document at -- at the bottom where Mr. Hadzic's signature appears that differentiates it from other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
